summary_md: **vveerrgg ([@vveerrgg](https://x.com/vveerrgg/status/2115211511824298284))** runs **DeepSeek V4.1 Flash** on stock llama.cpp by repacking ISTA-DASLab's GSQ-RCO quant into upstream GGUF format (byte-identical weights), reaching ~40 tok/s on one RTX PRO 6000 plus system RAM. Self-replies add an eval write-up (EVALS.md): against Unsloth's UD-IQ1_M in the same size class, GSM8K 97.2% vs 96.4% and MMLU 84.4% vs 84.6%, and against the full-precision API math was untouched.

relevance: Shows the max-tier DeepSeek running on upstream llama.cpp at low bit-width, with published quality comparisons.

media.description: Table comparing DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash 2-bit quants (ISTA GSQ-RCO IQ2_XXS, unsloth UD-IQ1_M) with full-precision DeepSeek API on 250 GSM8K and 500 MMLU questions, plus local decode speed on one RTX PRO 6000 plus RAM.

DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash: 2-bit quants vs full precision
Same 250 GSM8K and 500 MMLU questions · temperature 0 · thinking off
ISTA GSQ-RCO IQ2_XXS | unsloth UD-IQ1_M | DeepSeek API (full precision)
GSM8K (math): 97.2% | 96.4% | 96.8%
MMLU (knowledge): 84.4% | 84.6% | 87.0%
decode speed (1× RTX PRO 6000 + RAM): 31.9 tok/s | 24.3 tok/s | n/a
• GSM8K: all three are a statistical tie
• MMLU: full precision beats both quants (p < 0.05); the two quants tie each other
